paper_metadata.title: Quantum Computing: Implications for Portfolio Managers

experiments.description: Demonstration of an optimal multiperiod portfolio optimization problem formulated for a quantum annealer, using discrete integer holdings converted to a QUBO and evaluated on D-Wave hardware with repeated heuristic sampling.

algorithm.variant: quantum annealing for optimal multiperiod trading trajectory / portfolio optimization

hyperparameters.success_metric_alpha_percent: within α% of the optimal solution

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Discrete integer portfolio holdings are converted to binary variables for the QUBO formulation; the paper notes that the encoding choice affects the effective problem size (K, N, T) that can be solved.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Maximize portfolio return over a multiperiod trajectory while accounting for expected future return, risk, transaction costs, and permanent/temporary market impact; formulated as a QUBO min x^T Q x after suitable modifications.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Discrete integer holdings are encoded into binary variables; no explicit constraints are described in the QUBO form beyond the encoding and embedding.

problem_instance.description: Optimal multiperiod trading trajectory / portfolio optimization with transaction costs and market impact over a finite horizon.

dataset_specification.description: Illustrative example described as a four-asset universe over a time horizon of eight steps, with ten units invested at any given time; no real market dataset or ticker list is provided.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Forecasts of expected future returns and risk are assumed as inputs; no further preprocessing details are reported.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Each problem is solved 200 times on the quantum annealer; the most frequently obtained solution is taken as final. Success is measured by whether the solution is within α% of the optimal solution.

noise_model.noise_parameters: Quantum annealer operated at 12–17 milliKelvin and housed in shielding against electrical and magnetic interference.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Problem is embedded into the annealing chip and tuned via hardware settings; discrete integer variables are converted to binary QUBO form.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Multiple anneals are run and the most frequently observed solution is selected as the final answer.

speedup_claims.conditions: conceptual comparison for a 1152-qubit annealer; assumes one binary variable per qubit
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a conceptual statement, not a measured runtime speedup; actual usable problem size is much smaller due to embedding and hardware constraints.

speedup_claims.conditions: for a very specific type of optimization problem, as reported by Google in 2015
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this result is for a very specific optimization problem; general optimization problems were still under evaluation.

speedup_claims.conditions: for certain applications in machine learning, operations research, and optimization
speedup_claims.caveats: Stated as an expectation/prospect rather than a demonstrated result.
